belief: Jesus is one good way to God among many.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that Jesus is just one good way to God among many, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: A culture that values tolerance and says every path leads to the same place. Friends or family of other faiths whom you love and respect. Fear of seeming narrow or judgmental. Teachers or media that present Jesus only as a wise moral teacher. Discomfort with what Jesus’ claims mean for people you care about.
teaches: Jesus did not present Himself as one teacher among many. He said He is the way, the truth, and the life, and that no one comes to the Father except through Him. The apostles taught that salvation is found in no other name. This is not arrogance on our part. It is God’s gracious provision: He sent His Son so that anyone, from any background, can come to Him through Christ.
self_statements: All religions are basically the same.
It doesn’t matter what you believe as long as you’re sincere.
Saying Jesus is the only way is unloving.
Jesus was a great teacher, nothing more.
Good people will get to God however they choose.
I don’t want to seem narrow-minded.
errors: Deciding what is true based on what feels kind or comfortable.
Assuming that because religions share some values, they all lead to the same God.
Assuming people will see you as hateful if you believe Jesus’ own words.
Accepting Jesus’ moral teaching while ignoring what He said about Himself.
Believing you must choose between loving people and believing Jesus is the only way.
questions: What did Jesus Himself say about the way to the Father?
Can Jesus be only a good teacher if He claimed to be the only way?
Is something true because it feels tolerant, or because it is true?
Can I believe Jesus is the only way and still love and respect people of other faiths?
Why would God send His Son to die if there were many other ways?
Have I let culture, rather than Scripture, shape this belief?
What does the evidence of Jesus’ resurrection suggest about His claims?
truth: Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life. God has provided one sure way to Himself, and it is open to everyone through Christ. I can hold this truth with humility and love, respecting and caring for people of every background while pointing them to the Savior who welcomes all who come.
hw_questions: What did Jesus Himself say about the way to God?
Can a mere “good teacher” claim to be the only way?
Is this true, or does it just feel tolerant?
Can I believe this and still love people of other faiths?
Why would Jesus die if there were other ways?
Has culture or Scripture shaped my view?
hw_truths: Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life.
Salvation is found in Christ, and it is open to everyone.
I can hold this truth with humility and love.
God provided a sure way to Himself through His Son.
Believing Jesus does not require me to look down on anyone.
Whoever has the Son has life.
log: Each day, read one thing Jesus said about Himself in the Gospel of John and write it down.
name_example: I am the gate. If Sarah enters through Me, she will be saved. She will come in and go out and find pasture.
actions: Read the Gospel of John, chapters 14 and 15,
and underline every statement Jesus makes about who He is.
with someone of another faith, listening first, then sharing kindly what Jesus means to you.
to the question: “Who do you say that I am?” (Matthew 16:15).
“How do you hold this belief with love?” Write down what they say.
tracker: One thing Jesus said about Himself
prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the way, the truth, and the life. Help me reject the lie that You are only one path among many. Give me confidence in Your words and humility in how I share them. Fill me with love for people of every background, and let my life point them to You. In Your name, Amen.
songs: Jesus is the risen Savior and the source of salvation.
Christ’s sacrifice and rescue are the foundation of hope and access to God.
Jesus is present in suffering and is greater than the circumstances we face.
This classic hymn connects God’s greatness, Christ’s sacrifice, and future hope.
